topic: Morning phone use as a dopamine miscalibration trigger
body:
**You open your phone within 30 seconds of waking up. The day is already compromised before it starts.**

Here's the mechanism. Your brain wakes up in a low-stimulation state. That state is actually optimal — your prefrontal cortex is warming up, your dopamine baseline is clean. It's the best cognitive window you have all day.

The second you open a feed, you spike that baseline. Notifications, thumbnails, someone else's opinion — your brain reads all of it as high-reward input before you've done a single thing of value.

Now the problem. Every task you attempt after that has to compete with the stimulation level you just set. A work document doesn't compete. A hard problem doesn't compete. Your actual goals don't compete.

You haven't failed at discipline. You've miscalibrated the starting point.

The first hour of your day sets the dopamine floor everything else has to beat.

Put the phone in a different room tonight. Not on silent. In a different room. That single architectural change removes the decision entirely.

If you want the full reset protocol, it's in the link in bio.
